- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is conservative, slightly increase the low end to avoid underestimating downside.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., 3–5 days post-peak), apply a 3–5 day lag correction by subtracting 1–2% per day.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction of 1–3% to the next 30-day forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3) and forecast deviates >2% from true, adjust toward historical mean of last 7–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), reduce forecast slope toward historical trend.
